hero.title: Stop prompting. Start a [daily loop] with your {agent.}
hero.lede: Matt Pocock's skills are “for real engineers, straight from his .agents directory.” Each one does a single job. This page shows the order to use them through a normal workday, with example sessions for the four situations you'll hit most.
hero.installNote: Pick one install per agent, otherwise you get every skill twice. Then run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` once in each repo.

terminal.you: /grill-with-docs I want users to save a search and get alerts

terminal.q: Q1. Is a "saved search" just the text, or the text plus filters?

terminal.you: text + filters, dietary only for now

terminal.q: Q2. Where should the alert show up?

loop.title: One loop, five stops
loop.lede: Every change goes round the same loop. You trigger the main skills yourself with a slash command. Helper skills join in automatically when the agent needs them.

flow.title: The day as a branching map
flow.lede: Drawn like a git-flow diagram. Time runs down, and each lane is a place work lives: your conversation, the docs, the tracker, branches and `main`. Dots are skill runs or files written. Arrows show what feeds what.
flow.hint: Scroll sideways to see all six lanes.

day.title: What a normal day looks like
day.lede: An example day building one feature. The times are only illustrative. The order is the part that matters.

sessions.title: Four example sessions
sessions.lede: Pick a situation. On the left is the chain of skills. On the right is a shortened conversation showing how the session goes.
sessions.note: These are illustrative sessions, shortened to show the shape. Real skill output is longer and depends on your repo.

picker.title: Which skill do I need right now?
picker.lede: Choose what's happening. If none of these fit, `/ask-matt` routes you to the right skill.

catalog.title: All {count} skills on one page
catalog.lede: **User-invoked** skills are the ones you type. They orchestrate. **Model-invoked** skills are tools the agent picks up when they fit.

principles.title: Grill before every change
principles.text: The questions are cheap. Fixing wrong assumptions after the code exists costs far more.

principles.title: Keep the glossary alive
principles.text: When you and the agent use the same words, misunderstandings drop. `/wait-what` re-explains a confusing reply using those words.

principles.title: Fix the environment, not the prompt
principles.text: When something goes wrong, `/retro` turns it into a permanent fix in CLAUDE.md, tests or tooling.
